This methodological framework addresses the fundamental duality in basketball: offense accounts for roughly half of a player's value, while defense accounts for the other half. By isolating these contributions, analysts can identify undervalued players like Lamar Odom (+13) whose defensive improvements inflate their overall ratings. However, this additive model fails when defensive schemes drastically alter offensive efficiency, as seen in matchups where Marquis Daniels struggled against Manu Ginobili. The key failure mode occurs in playoff series when specific head-to-head matchups create non-linear interactions that the simple sum cannot capture.
